cases.prompt: A plant lead asks: which order ran on the line yesterday and how many defects did it have? We have machine time-series and a part counter but no idea how to tie it to orders. Where do we start?
cases.expected_output: Restates the request as object (order), event (defect recorded) and time axis (report on a cadence). Classifies each signal as sensor value, source event, derived event or identifier. Checks the object relation first and names the identifier source or routes a data gap. Does not approximate the order from timestamps and call it traced.

cases.prompt: The plant asks which carrier is in the oven right now. They have an oven temperature and a carrier id string in the data. What do we need from the data side?
cases.expected_output: Marks the temperature as a sensor value, not an event, and the entry and exit signals as events. Treats the carrier id as an object identifier. Names the carrier-to-part relation as a gap if only manual. Sets an archetype class and drafts the data requirements statement; open items stay to-confirm.

cases.prompt: Management wants a per-serial trace for one legacy line, tied to one old system, and says we can promise a root cause analysis from the vibration sensor. Please confirm.
cases.expected_output: Classifies the case as unique and says impact analysis comes first, decided by the OD lead or DBVE. Refuses to promise an analysis on a derived event whose method is not named. Lists what the key user must confirm.

cases.prompt: What should we call the part counter signal so that two plants can compare it?
cases.expected_output: Does not do object and event modelling. Routes the naming question to the signal standardization skill and mentions the data-requirements handoff only if relevant.
